title: bug: create_task stores order unchecked, and nextTaskOrder (unlike nextEpicOrder) does not skip non-finite orders, so one non-numeric order makes every later default-order row in that epic NaN (null on disk) and breaks epic-final detection
description:
Filed by the governor at 22:38Z on 2026-11-03 from hunt #12's held items (task-f6f0b580; architect-1dd28c7c's report msg-7098bc70). It waits on task-c90b41f1, which edits the same two files (createTask.ts, taskStore.ts). Promote it when c90b41f1 is DONE.

PROBLEM. create_task passes `params.order` straight into the task (createTask.ts:166 at tip 2f03c0f6). The default order comes from nextTaskOrder (taskStore.ts:844-848): `Math.max(...tasks.map((t) => t.order)) + 1` over every row in the epic, with no finiteness filter. So one non-numeric order makes every later default-order row in that epic NaN, which JSON writes as null. Its siblings already guard both halves:
- create_epic refuses a bad order with INVALID_INPUT (context.field 'order'), fixed in 68a47060.
- nextEpicOrder (StateManager.ts:1471-1479) skips non-finite orders, with a comment naming this exact failure.
It matters beyond sorting: epic-final detection (isEpicFinalTask in delivery/policy.ts) picks the epic's highest-order row, so a NaN order takes the "final integration row" status, and with it the full verification gate, away from the newest row.

EVIDENCE. Hunt repro /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_createTaskOrder.test.ts, run at f159784e and re-run by the hunt holder (me/me-zzHuntA_createTaskOrder.log): 4 failed, 1 passed.
- sibling: create_epic refuses order "abc" (PASS).
- r1: create_task accepts order "abc" and resolves success:true.
- r2: the next default-order task gets order NaN, and the disk holds null.
- r3: a legacy row with order "x" on disk makes the next default NaN instead of 3.
- r4: the epic's newest default-order row is no longer epic-final after one string order.
The board holds no such row today: I scanned 960 task files at 22:37Z and found 0 non-finite orders. That is why this is LOW.

FIX DIRECTION (the planner decides). In create_task, refuse an order that is present but not a finite number with coded INVALID_INPUT (context.field 'order'), before any write. Do NOT copy create_epic's integer rule: task orders on this board are fractional (231.164, 434.7, 440.7), and placement relies on that. Make nextTaskOrder skip non-finite orders the way nextEpicOrder does. Port the hunt repro into a test file of the row's own. Sync the `### moe.create_task` section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md with the new refusal (ruling msg-71db57ac: each row syncs its own tool section).
definitionOfDone: create_task refuses a present order that is not a finite number ("abc", NaN, Infinity, null, an object) with coded INVALID_INPUT naming field 'order', before any task is written, and still accepts fractional orders such as 231.164; docs/MCP_SERVER.md's `### moe.create_task` section names the refusal.

nextTaskOrder skips non-finite stored orders the way nextEpicOrder does, so a legacy non-numeric order on disk no longer yields a NaN/null default order and the epic's newest default-order row stays epic-final; a vitest file of the row's own proves the hunt repro's r1-r4 cases green.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 2. packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts nextTaskOrder (~:844-848): skip non-finite stored orders, exactly as StateManager.nextEpicOrder (~:1471-1479) does. Collect `.map((t) => t.order).filter((o) => typeof o === 'number' && Number.isFinite(o))` over the epic's tasks, return 1 when none is left, else Math.max(...orders) + 1.

Carry over nextEpicOrder's comment: a legacy or hand-edited non-numeric order made every later default NaN, which JSON writes as null. It also took epic-final status (isEpicFinalTask, delivery/policy.ts:240, maps non-finite orders to 0 and fails on a NaN own order) away from the epic's newest default-order row.

Finite-order epics get byte-identical results, so StateManager.test.ts's existing `describe('nextTaskOrder')` (~:1118-1140) must pass unchanged. Error handling: there is no new throw path; an epic whose rows all have non-finite orders gets 1, as an empty epic does. Tests come in step 3.

DoD 1, 2. New test file packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.order.test.ts, the row's own.

Port the hunt repro /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_createTaskOrder.test.ts. It uses ToolTestHarness with epic-1, task-a order 1, task-b order 2. Keep its cases:
- sibling: create_epic refuses 'abc'.
- r1: create_task refuses 'abc' with `{ codeName: 'INVALID_INPUT', context: { field: 'order' } }`.
- r2: after that refusal, the next default-order task has a finite order equal to its on-disk value.
- r3: a legacy row with order 'x' on disk gives the next default 3.
- r4: the newest default-order row is epic-final and task-b is not.

Add these cases:
- (a) A refusal matrix: 'abc', '1', NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, null, {}, [] and true. Each one is refused INVALID_INPUT with field 'order', and nothing is written: the task count, the .moe/tasks file listing and the TASK_CREATED emits are all unchanged. Reuse createTask.shape.test.ts's no-write assertions from c90b41f1.
- (b) Fractional and edge finite orders are accepted and stored exactly in memory and on disk: 231.164, 0, -2.5.
- (c) nextTaskOrder through state.nextTaskOrder: rows with order null and 'x' on disk are skipped, so the result is max finite + 1. An epic whose only rows are non-finite gives 1.

Use mutation-resistant toBe/toMatchObject assertions, never bare truthiness.

Red first: with createTask.ts and taskStore.ts at HEAD, r1-r4 and the matrix must fail. Note the counts in the completion summary. Error handling is what this file proves: every refusal path is coded and leaves no partial write.

DoD 1 (docs, ruling msg-71db57ac: this row syncs its own `### moe.create_task` section).

In docs/MCP_SERVER.md, `### moe.create_task` (~:1824), add one bullet to the **Input refusals** list after the taskRails bullet (~:1851):

"- an `order` that is present (`null` included) but not a finite number, e.g. a string, `null`, `NaN`, `Infinity` or an object. Fractional and negative orders such as `231.164` are accepted."

In the Parameters block, extend `order?: number,` with this comment: `// finite; omitted = one more than the epic's highest finite order (non-finite stored orders are skipped)`.

The verification grep reads the phrase 'not a finite number' from this section. Touch nothing else in the file. The existing sentence 'Each is INVALID_INPUT naming the field' already covers the code.

Verification: run this once, fresh, before complete_task. It is the narrow suite for this mid-epic slice, run on a snapshot outside the repo per the live-runtime rail:

`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && awk '$0=="### moe.create_task"{p=1;next} p&&/^### /{exit} p' docs/MCP_SERVER.md | grep -q 'not a finite number' && S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon docs/roles | tar -x -C "$S" && cp --parents packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.ts packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.order.test.ts "$S" && cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" NO_COLOR=1 sh -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null 2>&1 && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/tools/createTask.order.test.ts src/tools/createTask.shape.test.ts src/tools/createTask.test.ts src/state/StateManager.test.ts src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts src/tools/createEpic.validation.test.ts'`

What it covers:
- tsc confirms the `order?: unknown` narrowing.
- StateManager.test.ts carries the existing nextTaskOrder tests.
- qaApprove.test.ts exercises isEpicFinalTask.
- docs/roles is archived because some daemon tests read it.

Submit the exit code and output tail as complete_task evidence.
